newsitem.title: FRANCE: French utilities start working hours talks.
newsitem.headline: French utilities start working hours talks.

text.p: The chairmen of the French state-owned electricity company EDF and gas company GDF on Monday told labour unions that they had decided to open talks about employment and the reduction of working hours.

Edmond Alphandery, a former Economy Minister, and Pierre Gadonneix have "asked Jean-Louis Mathias, director of staff and social relations at both companies, to engage in talks on employment and working hours with the unions CGT, CFDT, Force Ouvriere, CGC and CFTC," a spokeswoman for EDF said.
"The aim is to increase the companies' capacity to hire young people and the development of the companies," she added.
Alphandery and Gadonneix have said in the past they want their companies' customer services and repair units to be available during more hours and days in the week through more work flexibility.
According to the Le Monde newspaper, EDF-GDF will propose a reduction of the working week to 32 hours, paid at 34 or 36, from 38 hours currently.
